title: ARRANGER_REMI tokenizer round-trip proof over real PDMX MIDI (Wave Q, Q-05)
gate: The training plan's first gate: no full training before the tokenizer is proven lossless modulo the grid on real data.

vocabulary.shape: REMI-style metrical events, plus per-track structure an arranger needs: Track_<family> opens each instrument's events; Tempo_<bin> and TimeSig_<n>/<d> are in the stream.
vocabulary.note: Lossy by quantization and by nothing else. Onset and duration snap to the grid; pitch, track family and bar index are exact.

run.corpus: .pdmx-data/mid — 254,035 MIDI files extracted from mid.tar.gz (verified md5)
run.sampling: reservoir sample with a fixed seed, so the run is reproducible

result.reading: Across 3,663,115 notes in 7,997 real scores, not one note was dropped and not one was invented. Every note round-tripped matching family, bar, position, pitch, velocity bin and duration bin. The only change is timing: a mean snap of 0.0012 of a quarter note (~0.6 ms at 120 BPM), never more than half a grid step, which is the grid doing exactly what it is for.

bugTheRealDataCaught.bug: Real PDMX scores carry time signatures the vocabulary did not: the first run threw on TimeSig_1/4.
bugTheRealDataCaught.fix: normaliseTimeSig folds any metre onto the nearest representable one by bar length, and the round-trip result carries a timeSigApproximated flag.
bugTheRealDataCaught.howOften: 3,423 of 7,997 files (43%) had their metre folded — mostly /8 and /2 variants and odd metres. Their notes still round-trip losslessly; only the bar-length label is approximate.

honestLimits: This proves the tokenizer preserves the notes. It does not prove the tokenization is good FOR LEARNING — that only the trained model can show.
43% of files had their time signature approximated. A model trained on this sees a slightly wrong bar length for those; the flag lets a training run weight or exclude them.

The grid is 12 steps per quarter. Genuinely rubato or heavily swung human performance would lose its microtiming here — which is correct for a symbolic arranger and wrong for a groove model. PDMX is notated scores, so this is not a concern for this corpus.
Percussion is mapped to a single 'drums' family. The specific drum voice (kick vs snare vs hat) survives as its MIDI pitch, but the tokenizer does not model a kit's structure.
No model has been trained. This is gate 1 of 5 (tokenizer round-trip -> dataset rights proof -> tiny overfit -> pilot -> benchmark).
